- PLAN-DEVIATION: Task 3 says to "use the harness's existing envelope-on-disk resume if present". It exists but is unsafe for this run: `runMatrixCell` skips any cell whose `runs/<cell>.json` is non-empty, and that file is the raw `claude -p --output-format json` stdout, which is written (non-empty) even when the child exits on `--max-budget-usd`/`--max-turns` or an error (`is_error: true`). A re-run therefore SKIPS budget-killed cells instead of retrying them, and the judge then scores an error result as recall 0 — biasing against whichever arm hits its cap (Fable at $20 is the likelier one). Corrected behaviour: resume only when the out file parses and `is_error !== true` (and, ideally, `subtype === "success"`); otherwise re-run. Same for `runJudgeCell`.

Do the routing work first (Task 4 then 5) because it is self-contained and test-driven: add `product` to `REVIEW_LENS_NAMES`, a `pinned-opus` member + `fallbackRow` case in `bin/lib/model-routing-table.ts`, branch the lens `.map` on `lens === "product"`, then add the `/"opus"/` parser branch ahead of `/inherited/` in `model-routing-table.test.ts` and bump both 16→17 counts (routing-table AND `config-models.test.ts`); for Task 5 add optional `effortPin` honoured first in `resolveRouting`, a `wantEffort` field in `AGENT_FRONTMATTER_POLICY`, and update the four every-row effort tests, keeping `flow-pr-review/SKILL.md` net-zero (1 line of headroom). In parallel do Task 1 inside the existing sub-agent `walkFile` callback of `docs/eval/token-spend-audit.ts`, and Task 2 in `run.ts` — but extend Task 2 to (i) make resume skip only successful, non-error out files and (ii) give `score.ts`'s non-committed path the per-PR + separation stats (reusing `exactPermutationP`) with a `score.test.ts` case, since Task 3's verdict rule cannot be computed from the current arms aggregate. Run Task 3 in a fresh data dir with both `gh pr view/diff` inputs and `materialize` ref sets, read model ids from `runs/*.json` `modelUsage`, then write Task 6 from the measured numbers.

## anti_patterns

- Off-limits (excluded path): capping discovery/planning at Opus on Fable sessions — the user keeps planning on the session model by deliberate choice; do not touch the `planning`/`scout`/`coder`/epic-designer `inherited` rows or `flow-product-critic`.
- Off-limits (excluded path): putting the product lens under `session-capped-opus` like the other lenses — on a Sonnet session the cap returns Sonnet, but the user asked for Opus on every session. It must be a distinct literal `pinned-opus` fallback.
- Rejected (excluded path): ranking/arguing the lever on per-turn multiples (2.3x/2.4–3.8x) — per finished task Fable discovery is ~15% over Opus 5; the analysis row must use per-run figures.
- Foreclosed shortcut: raising the `flow-pr-review/SKILL.md` line ceiling (1940) to fit the prose — it has 1 line of headroom and the plan requires net-zero edits.
- Foreclosed shortcut: trusting `run.ts`'s current resume to "skip completed cells" after a budget/rate-limit failure — a non-empty error envelope counts as completed, silently scoring failed cells as zero recall.
- Foreclosed shortcut: reading the resolved model id from `*.envelope.json` — it echoes the alias passed on the CLI, so the assertion would pass vacuously.
- Foreclosed shortcut: running `fable,opus` into the old sonnet/opus data dir, or quoting the new run against the committed 4.8% Opus recall without re-checking reference-set counts — `judgedArms` would mix three arms, and prompts are extracted live from today's `agent-prompts.md`, so only same-run arms are comparable.
- Rejected approach: using `flow-model-bench` as-is for (c) — it is agy/Gemini-only (`flow-delegate` transport); bolting a Claude transport onto it is the dropped old Task 2 and out of scope.
- Rejected approach: importing `exactPermutationP` from `score.ts` into `score-arms.ts` — `score.ts` already imports `score-arms.ts`, creating a cycle; compute separation in `score.ts` or move the helper.
- Pattern to avoid: a parser branch for `"opus"` placed after `/inherited/` — the product cell's "NOT inherited" text would misclassify it as `inherited` and the drift lint would fail to match (or match the wrong site).
- Off-limits git surface: the worktree shows ` D node_modules` — HEAD tracks `node_modules` as a symlink (`120000`, → `../flow/node_modules`) but the worktree has a real directory; `.gitignore`'s `node_modules/` does not cover the tracked symlink. Never `git add -A` / `git commit -a`; stage explicit paths only (the untrack fix lives on the unmerged `fix/untrack-node-modules-symlink` branch, `062e2b1`).
- Off-limits: the eight Task-tool exemption openers and "Load the Task tool before spawning" preambles that `model-routing.md` L7–10 says stay byte-exact — adding an Opus pin on an existing fan-out is not a new spawn site; don't restate or edit those blocks.
- Dependency to avoid: running the recall matrix from CI/`npm run verify` or adding it to PATH — the harness README declares it hand-run only (≈$48 for the full committed matrix).
